findings.description: MEAL_SLOT_IDS Set and _isCompatible() function are defined identically in both drag.js (lines 123-129) and mobile.js (lines 20-27). This duplication was introduced in this diff: drag.js added MEAL_SLOT_IDS as a new constant while mobile.js added both MEAL_SLOT_IDS and _isCompatible() as new additions. The two implementations are byte-for-byte identical and must be kept in sync manually.
findings.recommendation: Extract MEAL_SLOT_IDS and _isCompatible() into a shared module (e.g., web/js/slot-compat.js) and import from both drag.js and mobile.js. This is a pure refactor with no behavioral change.

findings.description: A third copy of the meal-slot key array is introduced: MEAL_SLOT_KEYS (local const inside _buildMealsCandidateGroup, line 182) and MEAL_SLOT_KEYS_ARR (module-level const, line 569) both equal ["breakfast", "lunch", "dinner"]. The module-level MEAL_SLOTS Set (line 39) already encodes this same set. Three representations of the same constant now coexist in state.js, all introduced in this diff.
findings.recommendation: Remove MEAL_SLOT_KEYS (local) and MEAL_SLOT_KEYS_ARR and derive the ordered array from the existing NAMED_SLOTS / MEAL_SLOTS constants: const MEAL_SLOT_KEYS_ARR = NAMED_SLOTS.filter(k => MEAL_SLOTS.has(k)). This eliminates two of the three duplicates.

summary.assessment: 5 critical violations, all provably introduced in this diff. Three are untokenised hardcoded hex colors in main.css (the Notion redesign removed the --primary-hover token but introduced raw hex equivalents). Two are code-duplication violations: an identical _isCompatible() + MEAL_SLOT_IDS pair duplicated between drag.js and mobile.js, and three separate representations of the meal slot key array in state.js. No dangling references, no merge conflicts, no Chinese text, no python3 misuse.
